A producer reads a fixed test fixture and places message IDs on a durable queue. Each message contains only synthetic content and a lab campaign identifier. Worker processes claim jobs with a visibility timeout, render the fixture, and post it to the sink endpoint. Use a token bucket for the lab endpoint, for example a modest number of requests per second, and expose the current queue depth, successful deliveries, transient failures, permanent failures, and latency percentiles. Retry only explicit transient responses, with exponential backoff and a maximum attempt count; route exhausted jobs to a dead-letter queue for inspection. Idempotency keys prevent a worker crash from duplicating a delivery. Do not add address rotation, deceptive headers, open relays, proxy pools, or throttle evasion; those features turn a lab queue into a spam system. Keep the exercise reproducible by versioning the fixture, configuration, and run identifier, and delete synthetic payloads after the test. This gives an engineering team useful measurements for queue durability and retry behavior while leaving no path to contact unsuspecting people.
